title: Manta: Hybrid-Sensitive Type Inference Toward Type-Assisted Bug Detection for Stripped Binaries
problem: Type information is lost in stripped binaries, preventing static analyzers from using type information to improve analysis precision and prune infeasible paths. This significantly limits the effectiveness of static binary bug detection.
motivation: Enabling type-aware static analysis for stripped binaries improves bug detection precision and security of binaries used in embedded systems and IoT devices.
method: Manta recovers the type information that's removed from stripped binaries by using data-flow analysis—tracking how values flow through code—at multiple sensitivity levels (different degrees of strictness), which together catch type constraints that any single approach would miss. The inferred types then eliminate impossible function call targets and help find bugs more accurately.
key_novelty: It combines multiple sensitivity levels in data-flow analysis to infer types and find bugs in stripped binaries.
contributions: Hybrid-sensitive type inference achieving 78.7% precision and 97.2% recall for type inference
63.9% improvement in pruning infeasible indirect-call targets versus existing type analysis
Program slicing on binaries achieving 61.1% similarity to source-code based slicing
Discovered 86 developer-confirmed vulnerabilities in IoT firmware with 64 CVE/PSV IDs

metrics.other: 63.9% improvement in infeasible indirect-call pruning; 61.1% program slicing similarity

primary_theme: Type inference for binary security analysis
